content.text:
I've submitted the campaign. None of the La–Sb–O compositions I measured showed meaningful photoactivity under 2.4 eV light, so the pick is best of a flat, noise-level set rather than a real hit.

**Submitted best: index 16 (Sb fraction 0.36), EQE 0.0047%.** It was the only measured composition with a positive EQE.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.12 | −0.0004 |
| 12 | 0.26 | −0.0082 |
| 16 | 0.36 | **+0.0047** |
| 21 | 0.51 | ≈0 |
| 28 | 0.68 | −0.0012 |

- **Why the values are so low:** La–Sb oxides have wide band gaps, so 2.4 eV light is unlikely to be absorbed. All five readings sit around zero, and three are slightly negative, so they're probably measurement noise. The difference between index 16 and the others shouldn't be read as a real performance ranking.
- **How I spent the budget:** I used all 5 EQE measurements, spread from Sb 0.12 to 0.68. The line runs from 0.08 to 0.68, and each measured point is near one of the known compound compositions. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. With every result this flat, XRD phase identification wouldn't have pointed to a better composition to measure, and there was no EQE budget left to act on it anyway.
- **What's untested:** A narrow active window could still sit between the points I measured, for example around Sb 0.15–0.2 or 0.4–0.45. Five measurements across 29 candidates can't rule that out.
